source.title: Beyond Gaussian Initializations: Signal Preserving Weight Initialization for Odd-Sigmoid Activations
source.authors: Hyunwoo Lee; Hayoung Choi; Hyunju Kim

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests initialization effects on signal propagation and trainability with different measures and odd-sigmoid feedforward networks; it does not directly measure training classification error or gradient norms as training proceeds.
record.gate_note: Validation accuracy and initialization-time signal or gradient propagation are reported. The study does not report training classification error, so its results do not directly test V1. It uses fully connected networks without skip connections; it does not compare plain and residual networks.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 through activation-matched initialization comparisons in plain odd-sigmoid feedforward networks, measuring gradient propagation, validation learning curves and PINN losses. Its cross-initialization comparisons with batch normalization do not establish V6's matched-network speed or learning-rate effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their activation-aware diagonal-plus-noise initialization preserves forward signals and backward gradients more robustly than Gaussian initializations in deep, relatively narrow odd-sigmoid FFNNs. They also report lower PINN losses with appropriately scaled activations and successful training without BN in several settings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses diagonal-plus-Gaussian-noise weights calibrated for odd-sigmoid activations and compares them with Gaussian initialization schemes; it does not reproduce the claim's random-label or residual-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with depth, width, dataset, and activation scale. Gaussian initialization performance degrades in deep, narrow, or rescaled-activation settings; CIFAR validation performance changes at sufficiently large depths.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed initialization without BN matches or exceeds different initialization schemes using BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-aware structured initialization can substitute for BN in some deep odd-sigmoid FFNN settings; this comparison alone does not determine BN's causal effect on training speed.

record.problems: The relevant image-classification comparisons report validation accuracy, not training classification error. Several results are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The described image-classification settings use fully connected networks, and do not test residual shortcuts.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports many additional initialization, activation, dataset, depth, width, and scale comparisons. Only representative CIFAR depth/width comparisons and BN-related outcomes were retained; additional activation and scale panels and the remaining per-setting results in Table 1 and Figures 25–36 were omitted to keep the extraction bounded. Figure-only numerical values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in convolutional networks, including corrupted or random labels.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified very deep tanh and Fixup results.
Orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian weights, training 10,000-layer convolutional networks, and direct classification training-error or time-to-target comparisons.
Recovery above the initial stability threshold, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence below the threshold.
The text does not establish the direction of matched BN-versus-no-BN accuracy-speed comparisons. Higher tolerated learning rates due to BN and Fixup residual-network training are not tested.

missing.what: Direct layerwise gradient-norm comparison at initialization: proposed initialization preserves gradients in 1,000-layer tanh FFNNs across widths, whereas EOC and Gaussian comparators exhibit rapid decay at moderate widths.

Depth-by-noise-scale validation-accuracy comparison for tanh, 0.1 tanh and 10 tanh: the proposed initialization supports accurate learning over a broader region than EOC. Exact cell values are unavailable.

Forward activation distributions remain dispersed under the proposed initialization up to depth 10,000 and down to width 20, while EOC distributions concentrate. These are propagation results, not evidence of training at 10,000 layers.

Black–Scholes and Burgers PINN loss comparisons between proposed and EOC initialization with scaled tanh and softsign activations. The text reports lower losses with suitably scaled activations and the proposed initialization; individual scale outcomes require the figures.

record.verdict_notes: No V4 limits_scope verdict follows merely from changing validation performance at greater depth: V4 does not promise depth-invariant accuracy. The supplied text contains figure captions and qualitative descriptions but omits plotted values. No V6 verdict is justified by the reported cross-initialization BN comparisons.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including on corrupted or random labels, is not reported.
No two-layer teacher-student ReLU problem or width-above-teacher comparison.

No comparison with identity shortcuts and no report of training error increasing with depth. The paper does test initialization on deep networks without skip connections, but this does not test the version's shortcut claim.
No orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison or 10,000-layer convolutional networks. Results concern odd-sigmoid fully connected networks and proposed structured versus Gaussian initializations.
No above-stability learning-rate phase or sharpness measurements.
Does not test Fixup. Batch-normalization comparisons use validation accuracy, not a direct measure of training speed or tolerated learning-rate range.
